settings.html:
Conformance Status

The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) define requirements for designers and developers to improve accessibility for people with disabilities. It defines three levels of conformance: Level A, Level AA, and Level AAA. The AGFinancial website is fully conformant with WCAG Level A and partially conformant with WCAG Level AA.

Limitations

Limitations to WCAG Level AA conformance on the AGFinancial website may include color contrast. To increase the color contrast, follow these instructions according to your operating system:

  • Increase Contrast for Mac OS
  • Increase Contrast for Windows

Give Feedback

We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of our website. Please let us know if you encounter accessibility barriers by contacting us.

settings.bodyHtml: We're more than a financial partner. We're part of your ministry. It's our pleasure to design a loan with rates and flexible terms specifically for you. The loans lineup below might give you a great place to start.
settings.card1Body: Permanent, first-mortgage financing to help you purchase facilities or refinance existing loans. No short-sighted balloon notes that can leave your ministry financially vulnerable.
settings.card2Body: Designed exclusively for young, high-performing, growing churches to purchase a first permanent facility. This loan helps establish permanent roots, and leaves leasing in the past.
settings.card3Body: New construction or renovation financing, featuring interest-only payments during the project. After construction, a guaranteed, no-cost conversion to permanent financing.
settings.card4Body: Made for a quick win for "opportunity areas" (cracked parking lot, ancient carpet, music on cassette, etc.) while keeping cash in the bank and holding fundraising for larger future needs.
settings.card5Body: For large churches with a God-sized vision to buy a new campus, build a new facility, or refresh an existing building. Designed to be a 'war chest' of resources ready when God opens a door and time is of the essence.
settings.card6Body: Often, a parent-affiliated church (PAC) is an effective way to reach more of the larger geographic community. This financing package was created for a PAC to plant or revitalize a daughter church.
settings.card7Body: Precisely what its name implies, a credit line is a convenient, customized alternative for short-term expenses, smaller renovation projects, and ongoing cash flow needs.

settings.title: There's more to every loan.
settings.col1Body: Construction surprises usually aren't fun. Reducing those through front-of-project, detailed consultation has saved numerous churches hundreds of thousands of dollars in 'surprise' expenses and fees. Included with every construction loan.
settings.col2Body: We're part of your team. Your AGFinancial consultant is ready to answer questions, hear your dreams, listen to your concerns, and make it all as easy as possible. We don't do broker fees, so that relationship you experience? It's genuine.
settings.col3Body: Over the past 75+ years, AGFinancial has funded more than $1.6 billion in loans to an impressive variety of churches and ministries. Through it all, and just like you, we want to honor Jesus in our partnerships and how we do business.
settings.col4Body: A ministry returning to us for its next loan — and the next — really says something. Many of our borrowers are repeat clients. That's the best endorsement we could ask for.

settings.heading:
Tax benefits.
Ministry support.
Payments for life.
settings.bodyHtml: ...and payments that won't change with the market. Through a Charitable Gift Annuity (CGA), your generosity has the power to bless both the ministries and the people you love with fixed payments, charitable tax deductions, and attractive rates.
settings.body: ...and completely unaffected by the economy. Through a Charitable Gift Annuity (CGA), your generosity has the power to bless both the ministries and the people you love with fixed payments, potential tax deductions, and attractive rates.

settings.title: How it works
settings.col1Body: You fund the gift with cash or securities, and should receive an immediate charitable deduction.
settings.col2Body: AG Foundation invests those assets and pays you a fixed amount (according to your age) every year for the rest of your life.
settings.col3Body: When you pass away, a portion of the remainder goes to support ministry.

settings.title: It starts with your gift.
settings.card1Body:
• Cash (a significant portion of the annuity income may be tax-free)
  • Appreciated securities (may avoid a portion of capital gains tax)
  • $10,000 minimum

The SECURE 2.0 Act allows you to fund a Charitable Gift Annuity with funds distributed from your IRA up to $50,000* of your annual Qualified Charitable Distribution limit (QCD). This charitable distribution amount is both retirement income for you, and a gift of support to a ministry you choose. Even better, this distribution can count toward your IRA’s annual Required Minimum Distribution (RMD). You’re permitted to take advantage of this unique opportunity only once.

settings.html: The SECURE 2.0 Act allows you to fund a Charitable Gift Annuity with funds distributed from your IRA up to $50,000* of your annual Qualified Charitable Distribution limit (QCD). Even better, this distribution can count toward your IRA’s annual Required Minimum Distribution (RMD). You’re permitted to take advantage of this unique opportunity only once.
Also available for Charitable Remainder Unitrust (CRUT) or Charitable Remainder Annuity Trust (CRAT).
settings.fineprint:
*Indexed annually for inflation
**Also available for Charitable Remainder Unitrust (CRUT) or Charitable Remainder Annuity Trust (CRAT)
This is a one-time, lifetime opportunity; not available on an annual basis
Restrictions apply.

settings.title: Charitable Gift Annuity Options
settings.card1Body:
Start receiving payments **now**.

If you desire current income, you may transfer cash or securities in exchange for a contract for payment to begin within four weeks. You should receive a current income tax charitable deduction for the value of your gift to AG Foundation.
settings.card2Body:
Receive payments in the **future**.

Deferment compresses payout into a shorter time frame, so your annual payments will be higher than an immediate CGA. You should receive a current charitable income tax deduction.

settings.title: Charitable Remainder Trust
settings.bodyHtml: You contribute cash, stocks, real estate, or other assets to AG Foundation to establish the trust. The trust pays you (and your spouse, if married) income for life. You can also designate others, like children, to receive payments for up to 20 years. When the trust ends, the remaining assets go to the ministries you’ve selected.

settings.card1Bullets:
Annual payout is determined by donor
Account balance is revalued at the beginning of each year
Minimum required payout of 5%
Income may fluctuate from year to year
settings.card2Bullets:
Donor receives a fixed payment
Payment can be based on life expectancy or term of years
Payments may begin immediately upon funding

settings.title: Charitable Lead Trust
settings.bodyHtml: A Charitable Lead Trust works in the opposite way of a Charitable Remainder Trust. You contribute cash, stocks, real estate, or other assets to AG Foundation to establish the trust. The trust pays income to the ministry(ies) you’ve selected for a set number of years. When the trust ends, the remaining assets return to you or transfer to your family—often with significant growth in value.

settings.card1Bullets:
Donor receives remainder of trust after stated period of time
Charitable income tax deduction (equal to the total value of the income payments to ministry) is given in the year the trust is created
Donor is taxed on the trust’s income each year
settings.card2Bullets:
A named beneficiary, ministry, or heirs receive remainder of trust after predetermined payout period
Permanent transfer of asset
Reduces gift or estate tax and removes asset from estate
Income is taxed at the trust level each year

settings.html:
403(b) Plan Loans

A 403(b) loan allows you to borrow money from your own retirement savings without incurring early withdrawal tax penalties. The interest paid on this type of loan goes back into your retirement savings. Though convenient, this type of loan can significantly impact your retirement savings growth.

Details

The requested 403(b) loan amount cannot be less than $1,500. In addition, the amount borrowed cannot exceed the lesser of:

  • 100% of the total vested account balance if less than $10,000
  • 50% of the total vested account balances
  • or $50,000

Contact your AGFinancial retirement consultant for more information.

Members may have no more than two loans at a time. The interest rate for plan loans is fixed for the life of the loan at 2.0% above the rate of the MBA Income Fund. All loan payments are made by automatic bank draft on the 20th of each month. The maximum term of a loan is 59 months (5 years) regardless of intended use.

Due to regulations issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, 403(b) plan loans issued after Dec. 31, 2008 require employer verification of loan qualifications with the following exception: your employer has a sole service provider agreement with Ministers Benefit Association, and has not had multiple service providers since 2004.

settings.title: 403(b) Compliance Regulations
settings.bodyHtml:
The Internal Revenue Service issued regulations on 403(b) plans that generally became effective on January 1, 2009. These regulations impact all 403(b) plans and require a written plan document that contains the material plan provisions. If AGFinancial is your exclusive service provider, compliance implementation can be easier. Compliance may be more complex if you use multiple providers.

403(b) Guidelines of Administrative Responsibilities

AGFinancial and MBA provide multiple administrative functions for compliance with regulations; however, some administrative functions remain your responsibility as the employer fiduciary. Download the checklist that matches your organization type.

This information is not legal or tax advice. Work with your ministry’s legal and tax advisors to ensure you have satisfied all IRS 403(b) regulation requirements.

settings.bodyHtml: Tax advantages and a broad range of investment options can anchor your retirement savings. Whether you’re starting a nest egg or adding to existing plans, an IRA may be the perfect fit for your needs and goals.
settings.body: Tax advantages and a broad range of investment options can anchor your retirement savings. Whether you’re starting a nest egg or adding to existing plans, an IRA may be the perfect fit for your needs and goals.

settings.card1Body: A Traditional IRA lets your contributions and earnings grow tax-deferred. You won’t pay taxes on them until you withdraw the money in retirement. This allows your savings to compound faster over time, plus your contributions are deductible on your tax returns.
settings.card2Body: A Roth IRA lets your savings grow completely tax-free. Unlike a Traditional IRA, you pay taxes on your contributions now, but in retirement you can withdraw everything—including all your earnings—without paying any taxes.

settings.body: AGFinancial is committed to ensuring visitors with disabilities have the same quality of access to all the information on our website as non-disabled visitors. We are continually improving the user experience for everyone and applying updates to meet or exceed accessibility standards.

settings.html:
Conformance Status

The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) define requirements for designers and developers to improve accessibility for people with disabilities. It defines three levels of conformance: Level A, Level AA, and Level AAA. The AGFinancial website is fully conformant with WCAG Level A and partially conformant with WCAG Level AA.

Limitations

Limitations to WCAG Level AA conformance on the AGFinancial website may include color contrast. To increase the color contrast, follow these instructions according to your operating system:

  • Increase Contrast for Mac OS
  • Increase Contrast for Windows

Give Feedback

We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of our website. Please let us know if you encounter accessibility barriers by contacting us.

Collection and Use of Personal Information

AGFinancial collects nonpublic personal information to administer accounts, process transactions, and provide requested services.

Information may come from applications, transactions, agents, and communications.

settings.subtitle: Longer term rates with shorter term access
settings.body: Laddering splits your savings into multiple certificates that mature at different times. That gives you regular access to cash while you pursue longer-term rates.

settings.title: Every loan, 100% customized.
settings.subtitle: You won't find this at a bank.
settings.bodyHtml: We're more than a financial partner. We're part of your ministry. It's our pleasure to design a loan with rates and flexible terms specifically for you. The loans lineup below might give you a great place to start.
settings.card1Body: Permanent, first-mortgage financing to help you purchase facilities or refinance existing loans. No short-sighted balloon notes that can leave your ministry financially vulnerable.
settings.card2Body: Designed exclusively for young, high-performing, growing churches to purchase a first permanent facility. This loan helps establish permanent roots, and leaves leasing in the past.
settings.card3Body: New construction or renovation financing, featuring interest-only payments during the project. After construction, a guaranteed, no-cost conversion to permanent financing.
settings.card4Body: Made for a quick win for "opportunity areas" (cracked parking lot, ancient carpet, music on cassette, etc.) while keeping cash in the bank and holding fundraising for larger future needs.
settings.card5Body: For large churches with a God-sized vision to buy a new campus, build a new facility, or refresh an existing building. Designed to be a 'war chest' of resources ready when God opens a door and time is of the essence.
settings.card6Body: Often, a parent-affiliated church (PAC) is an effective way to reach more of the larger geographic community. This financing package was created for a PAC to plant or revitalize a daughter church.
settings.card7Body: Precisely what its name implies, a credit line is a convenient, customized alternative for short-term expenses, smaller renovation projects, and ongoing cash flow needs.

settings.title: There's more to every loan.
settings.col1Body: Construction surprises usually aren't fun. Reducing those through front-of-project, detailed consultation has saved numerous churches hundreds of thousands of dollars in 'surprise' expenses and fees. Included with every construction loan.
settings.col2Body: We're part of your team. Your AGFinancial consultant is ready to answer questions, hear your dreams, listen to your concerns, and make it all as easy as possible. We don't do broker fees, so that relationship you experience? It's genuine.
settings.col3Body: Over the past 75+ years, AGFinancial has funded more than $1.6 billion in loans to an impressive variety of churches and ministries. Through it all, and just like you, we want to honor Jesus in our partnerships and how we do business.
settings.col4Body: A ministry returning to us for its next loan — and the next — really says something. Many of our borrowers are repeat clients. That's the best endorsement we could ask for.

settings.heading:

Payments for life.
settings.bodyHtml: ...and payments that won't change with the market. Through a Charitable Gift Annuity (CGA), your generosity has the power to bless both the ministries and the people you love with fixed payments, charitable tax deductions, and attractive rates.
settings.body: ...and completely unaffected by the economy. Through a Charitable Gift Annuity (CGA), your generosity has the power to bless both the ministries and the people you love with fixed payments, potential tax deductions, and attractive rates.

settings.title: How it works
settings.col1Body: You fund the gift with cash or securities, and should receive an immediate charitable deduction.
settings.col2Body: AG Foundation invests those assets and pays you a fixed amount (according to your age) every year for the rest of your life.
settings.col3Body: When you pass away, a portion of the remainder goes to support ministry.

settings.title: It starts with your gift.
settings.card1Body:
• Cash (a significant portion of the annuity income may be tax-free)
  • Appreciated securities (may avoid a portion of capital gains tax)
  • $10,000 minimum

The SECURE 2.0 Act allows you to fund a Charitable Gift Annuity with funds distributed from your IRA up to $50,000* of your annual Qualified Charitable Distribution limit (QCD). This charitable distribution amount is both retirement income for you, and a gift of support to a ministry you choose. Even better, this distribution can count toward your IRA’s annual Required Minimum Distribution (RMD). You’re permitted to take advantage of this unique opportunity only once.

Even better, this distribution can count toward your IRA’s annual Required Minimum Distribution (RMD). You’re permitted to take advantage of this unique opportunity only once.
Also available for Charitable Remainder Unitrust (CRUT) or Charitable Remainder Annuity Trust (CRAT).
settings.fineprint:
*Indexed annually for inflation
**Also available for Charitable Remainder Unitrust (CRUT) or Charitable Remainder Annuity Trust (CRAT)
This is a one-time, lifetime opportunity; not available on an annual basis
Restrictions apply.

settings.title: Charitable Gift Annuity Options
settings.card1Body:
Start receiving payments **now**.

If you desire current income, you may transfer cash or securities in exchange for a contract for payment to begin within four weeks. You should receive a current income tax charitable deduction for the value of your gift to AG Foundation.
settings.card2Body:
Receive payments in the **future**.

Deferment compresses payout into a shorter time frame, so your annual payments will be higher than an immediate CGA. You should receive a current charitable income tax deduction.

settings.title: Charitable Remainder Trust
settings.bodyHtml: You contribute cash, stocks, real estate, or other assets to AG Foundation to establish the trust. The trust pays you (and your spouse, if married) income for life. You can also designate others, like children, to receive payments for up to 20 years. When the trust ends, the remaining assets go to the ministries you’ve selected.

settings.card1Bullets:
Annual payout is determined by donor
Account balance is revalued at the beginning of each year
Minimum required payout of 5%
Income may fluctuate from year to year
settings.card2Bullets:
Donor receives a fixed payment
Payment can be based on life expectancy or term of years
Payments may begin immediately upon funding

settings.title: Charitable Lead Trust
settings.bodyHtml: A Charitable Lead Trust works in the opposite way of a Charitable Remainder Trust. You contribute cash, stocks, real estate, or other assets to AG Foundation to establish the trust. The trust pays income to the ministry(ies) you’ve selected for a set number of years. When the trust ends, the remaining assets return to you or transfer to your family—often with significant growth in value.

settings.card1Bullets:
Donor receives remainder of trust after stated period of time
Charitable income tax deduction (equal to the total value of the income payments to ministry) is given in the year the trust is created
Donor is taxed on the trust’s income each year
settings.card2Bullets:
A named beneficiary, ministry, or heirs receive remainder of trust after predetermined payout period
Permanent transfer of asset
Reduces gift or estate tax and removes asset from estate
Income is taxed at the trust level each year

settings.title: Annual Contribution Limits
fineprint: *Beginning in 2026, participants who have FICA wages exceeding $150,000 (adjusted for inflation) in the previous calendar year will be required to make any catch-up contributions on a Roth (after-tax) basis. It is the Employer’s responsibility to ensure contributions are correctly submitted to the Plan. Employees below the $150,000 threshold, as well as ministers who earn SECA wages may continue to make catch-up contributions on either a pre-tax or Roth basis, depending on your plan’s design.

**The rule applies to individuals who will attain age 60 in the taxable year and continues until the taxable year in which they turn 64. So, a participant would be eligible for the entire year in which they turn 60 (even if their birthday is December 31), and they would not be eligible in the year in which they turn 64.
***All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax. Cannot exceed includible compensation.

†All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax; amounts over the general overall limit must be age 50 catch-up deferrals. Cannot exceed includible compensation except to the extent that the age 50 or older catch-up deferral has been utilized.

settings.html:
403(b) Plan Loans

A 403(b) loan allows you to borrow money from your own retirement savings without incurring early withdrawal tax penalties. The interest paid on this type of loan goes back into your retirement savings. Though convenient, this type of loan can significantly impact your retirement savings growth.

Details

The requested 403(b) loan amount cannot be less than $1,500. In addition, the amount borrowed cannot exceed the lesser of:

  • 100% of the total vested account balance if less than $10,000
  • 50% of the total vested account balances
  • or $50,000

Contact your AGFinancial retirement consultant for more information.

Members may have no more than two loans at a time. The interest rate for plan loans is fixed for the life of the loan at 2.0% above the rate of the MBA Income Fund. All loan payments are made by automatic bank draft on the 20th of each month. The maximum term of a loan is 59 months (5 years) regardless of intended use.

Due to regulations issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, 403(b) plan loans issued after Dec. 31, 2008 require employer verification of loan qualifications with the following exception: your employer has a sole service provider agreement with Ministers Benefit Association, and has not had multiple service providers since 2004.

settings.title: 403(b) Compliance Regulations
settings.bodyHtml:
The Internal Revenue Service issued regulations on 403(b) plans that generally became effective on January 1, 2009. These regulations impact all 403(b) plans and require a written plan document that contains the material plan provisions. If AGFinancial is your exclusive service provider, compliance implementation can be easier. Compliance may be more complex if you use multiple providers.

403(b) Guidelines of Administrative Responsibilities

AGFinancial and MBA provide multiple administrative functions for compliance with regulations; however, some administrative functions remain your responsibility as the employer fiduciary. Download the checklist that matches your organization type.

This information is not legal or tax advice. Work with your ministry’s legal and tax advisors to ensure you have satisfied all IRS 403(b) regulation requirements.

For assistance, contact 800.622.7526 or email 403bregs@agfinancial.org.

settings.bodyHtml: Tax advantages and a broad range of investment options can anchor your retirement savings. Whether you’re starting a nest egg or adding to existing plans, an IRA may be the perfect fit for your needs and goals.
settings.body: Tax advantages and a broad range of investment options can anchor your retirement savings. Whether you’re starting a nest egg or adding to existing plans, an IRA may be the perfect fit for your needs and goals.

settings.card1Body: A Traditional IRA lets your contributions and earnings grow tax-deferred. You won’t pay taxes on them until you withdraw the money in retirement. This allows your savings to compound faster over time, plus your contributions are deductible on your tax returns.
settings.card2Body: A Roth IRA lets your savings grow completely tax-free. Unlike a Traditional IRA, you pay taxes on your contributions now, but in retirement you can withdraw everything—including all your earnings—without paying any taxes.

settings.heading: Your IRA can do more.
settings.bodyHtml: If you're 70½ or older, a Qualified Charitable Distribution (QCD) lets you transfer up to $110,000 per year directly to your church or an eligible ministry — tax-free, and straight from the source. It counts toward your required minimum distribution, and not a dollar goes to taxes first.
settings.body: If you're 70½ or older, a Qualified Charitable Distribution (QCD) lets you transfer up to $110,000 per year directly to your church or an eligible ministry — tax-free, and straight from the source. It counts toward your required minimum distribution, and not a dollar goes to taxes first.

settings.title: How it works
settings.col1Body: Tell your IRA administrator you'd like to make a QCD. They will initiate the direct transfer.
settings.col2Body: Choose where the gift goes—a church, a ministry, a 501(c)(3) organization—and decide the amount.
settings.col3Body: Because the distribution goes directly to the ministry, it's excluded from your taxable income entirely. Your generosity goes further.

settings.heading: All your charitable giving in one place.
settings.bodyHtml: A Donor Advised Fund (DAF) provides a convenient, tax-efficient way to manage your giving from tithing to disaster relief, and all donations in between. Our frictionless process makes even complex securities easier to give than ever.
settings.body: A Generosity Fund ® is a Donor Advised Fund (DAF) that provides a convenient, tax-efficient way to manage your giving from tithing to disaster relief, and all donations in between. Our frictionless process makes even complex securities easier to give than ever .

settings.title: How it works
settings.col1Body: Open a DAF, and fund it with cash or appreciated assets. You may receive immediate tax benefits.
settings.col2Body: AG Foundation takes it from there, keeping track of your giving while handling the details.
settings.col3Body: Advise us where to provide grants to continue giving when and to whom you want. You may even give anonymously.

settings.title: Annual Contribution Limits
fineprint: *Beginning in 2026, participants who have FICA wages exceeding $150,000 (adjusted for inflation) in the previous calendar year will be required to make any catch-up contributions on a Roth (after-tax) basis. It is the Employer’s responsibility to ensure contributions are correctly submitted to the Plan. Employees below the $150,000 threshold, as well as ministers who earn SECA wages may continue to make catch-up contributions on either a pre-tax or Roth basis, depending on your plan’s design.

**The rule applies to individuals who will attain age 60 in the taxable year and continues until the taxable year in which they turn 64. So, a participant would be eligible for the entire year in which they turn 60 (even if their birthday is December 31), and they would not be eligible in the year in which they turn 64.
***All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax. Cannot exceed includible compensation.

†All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax; amounts over the general overall limit must be age 50 catch-up deferrals. Cannot exceed includible compensation except to the extent that the age 50 or older catch-up deferral has been utilized.

Contact your own tax advisor before taking any action that would have a tax consequence. This information is not tax advice. Information is from sources deemed reliable. Information is subject to error, omission, withdrawal, or change.

settings.html:
403(b) Plan Loans

A 403(b) loan allows you to borrow money from your own retirement savings without incurring early withdrawal tax penalties. The interest paid on this type of loan goes back into your retirement savings. Though convenient, this type of loan can significantly impact your retirement savings growth.

Details

The requested 403(b) loan amount cannot be less than $1,500. In addition, the amount borrowed cannot exceed the lesser of:

  • 100% of the total vested account balance if less than $10,000
  • 50% of the total vested account balances
  • or $50,000

Contact your AGFinancial retirement consultant for more information.

Members may have no more than two loans at a time. The interest rate for plan loans is fixed for the life of the loan at 2.0% above the rate of the MBA Income Fund. All loan payments are made by automatic bank draft on the 20th of each month. The maximum term of a loan is 59 months (5 years) regardless of intended use.

Due to regulations issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, 403(b) plan loans issued after Dec. 31, 2008 require employer verification of loan qualifications with the following exception: your employer has a sole service provider agreement with Ministers Benefit Association, and has not had multiple service providers since 2004.

settings.title: Investment Laddering Strategy
settings.subtitle: Longer term rates with shorter term access
settings.body: Laddering splits your savings into multiple certificates that mature at different times. That gives you regular access to cash while you pursue longer-term rates.
settings.step1: Split your total into equal parts.
settings.step2: Start by buying certificates with staggered maturities (1-year, 2-year, 3-year...).
settings.step3: When one matures, either reinvest into your selected longest-term certificate to keep the ladder going, or take the maturity as cash.

settings.title: Annual Contribution Limits
fineprint: *Beginning in 2026, participants who have FICA wages exceeding $150,000 (adjusted for inflation) in the previous calendar year will be required to make any catch-up contributions on a Roth (after-tax) basis. It is the Employer’s responsibility to ensure contributions are correctly submitted to the Plan. Employees below the $150,000 threshold, as well as ministers who earn SECA wages may continue to make catch-up contributions on either a pre-tax or Roth basis, depending on your plan’s design.

**The rule applies to individuals who will attain age 60 in the taxable year and continues until the taxable year in which they turn 64. So, a participant would be eligible for the entire year in which they turn 60 (even if their birthday is December 31), and they would not be eligible in the year in which they turn 64.
***All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax. Cannot exceed includible compensation.

†All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax; amounts over the general overall limit must be age 50 catch-up deferrals. Cannot exceed includible compensation except to the extent that the age 50 or older catch-up deferral has been utilized.

Contact your own tax advisor before taking any action that would have a tax consequence. This information is not tax advice. Information is from sources deemed reliable. Information is subject to error, omission, withdrawal, or change.

settings.html:
403(b) Plan Loans

A 403(b) loan allows you to borrow money from your own retirement savings without incurring early withdrawal tax penalties. The interest paid on this type of loan goes back into your retirement savings. Though convenient, this type of loan can significantly impact your retirement savings growth.

Details

The requested 403(b) loan amount cannot be less than $1,500. In addition, the amount borrowed cannot exceed the lesser of:

  • 100% of the total vested account balance if less than $10,000
  • 50% of the total vested account balances
  • or $50,000

Contact your AGFinancial retirement consultant for more information.

Members may have no more than two loans at a time. The interest rate for plan loans is fixed for the life of the loan at 2.0% above the rate of the MBA Income Fund. All loan payments are made by automatic bank draft on the 20th of each month. The maximum term of a loan is 59 months (5 years) regardless of intended use.

Due to regulations issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, 403(b) plan loans issued after Dec. 31, 2008 require employer verification of loan qualifications with the following exception: your employer has a sole service provider agreement with Ministers Benefit Association, and has not had multiple service providers since 2004.

settings.card5Body: Select your plan and open the **Info** tab.
settings.card6Body: Under **Take Action On Your Account**, select **Loans**, and then **Request a Loan**.

settings.title: This is legacy planning and charitable giving made easy.
settings.card1Body: A Donor Advised Fund lets you contribute assets, receive an immediate tax deduction, and recommend grants to the ministries and causes you care about. It’s a tax-smart, flexible way to give on your own timeline.
settings.card2Body: Similar to a CGA, a Charitable Trust provides generous support for ministry while the donor receives potential tax benefits. You choose when to support the ministry: at the completion of the trust, or at its onset.
settings.card3Body: A popular planned gift that provides payments for you, a Charitable Gift Annuity (CGA) allows you to receive dependable lifetime fixed payments and leave a gift to the ministry of your choice.
settings.card4Body: This long-term, stable source of funding is designed to keep your gifted principal intact so it can grow over time. The annual investment income may be used for scholarships, ministries, or other purposes you specify.
settings.card5Body: Designed for churches to receive non-cash gifts of any type: stock, real estate, and more, a Ministry Impact Fund removes giving barriers and delivers cash directly to your ministry.
settings.card6Body: Creating a giving plan is not only a smart financial choice—it’s also a way to provide for your loved ones, gain potential tax savings, and bless the ministries close to your heart.
settings.card7Body: Simple and straightforward, a will ensures a distribution end-of-life plan for your assets. This service is provided free of charge when you designate a 10% gift to an Assemblies of God ministry.
settings.card8Body: Your IRA can do more than fund your retirement. If you’re 70½ or older, a Qualified Charitable Distribution (QCD) lets you transfer up to $110,000 per year directly to your church or an eligible ministry tax-free, and straight from the source.

settings.card2Title: Establish a plan as an employer.

settings.html:
403(b) Plan Loans

A 403(b) loan allows you to borrow money from your own retirement savings without incurring early withdrawal tax penalties. The interest paid on this type of loan goes back into your retirement savings. Though convenient, this type of loan can significantly impact your retirement savings growth.

Details

The requested 403(b) loan amount cannot be less than $1,500. In addition, the amount borrowed cannot exceed the lesser of:

  • 100% of the total vested account balance if less than $10,000
  • 50% of the total vested account balances
  • or $50,000

Contact your AGFinancial retirement consultant for more information.

Members may have no more than two loans at a time. The interest rate for plan loans is fixed for the life of the loan at 2.0% above the rate of the MBA Income Fund. All loan payments are made by automatic bank draft on the 20th of each month. The maximum term of a loan is 59 months (5 years) regardless of intended use.

Due to regulations issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, 403(b) plan loans issued after Dec. 31, 2008 require employer verification of loan qualifications with the following exception: your employer has a sole service provider agreement with Ministers Benefit Association, and has not had multiple service providers since 2004.

settings.title: How to apply
settings.card1Body: Review the loan rules.
settings.card2Body: Log in.
settings.card4Body: Click **Manage My Retirement** under **Retirement Details**.
settings.card5Body: Select your plan and open the **Info** tab.
settings.card6Body: Under **Take Action On Your Account**, select **Loans**, and then **Request a Loan**.

settings.bodyHtml: Tax advantages and a broad range of investment options can anchor your retirement savings. Whether you’re starting a nest egg or adding to existing plans, an IRA may be the perfect fit for your needs and goals.
settings.body: Tax advantages and a broad range of investment options can anchor your retirement savings. Whether you’re starting a nest egg or adding to existing plans, an IRA may be the perfect fit for your needs and goals.

settings.card1Body: A Traditional IRA lets your contributions and earnings grow tax-deferred. You won’t pay taxes on them until you withdraw the money in retirement. This allows your savings to compound faster over time, plus your contributions are deductible on your tax returns.
settings.card2Body: A Roth IRA lets your savings grow completely tax-free. Unlike a Traditional IRA, you pay taxes on your contributions now, but in retirement you can withdraw everything—including all your earnings—without paying any taxes.

fineprint: Contact your tax advisor. Additional AGFinancial early redemption penalties and IRA custodial fees may apply.

settings.bodyHtml: Tax advantages and a broad range of investment options can anchor your retirement savings. Whether you’re starting a nest egg or adding to existing plans, an IRA may be the perfect fit for your needs and goals.
settings.body: Tax advantages and a broad range of investment options can anchor your retirement savings. Whether you’re starting a nest egg or adding to existing plans, an IRA may be the perfect fit for your needs and goals.

settings.card1Body: A Traditional IRA lets your contributions and earnings grow tax-deferred. You won’t pay taxes on them until you withdraw the money in retirement. This allows your savings to compound faster over time, plus your contributions are deductible on your tax returns.
settings.card2Body: A Roth IRA lets your savings grow completely tax-free. Unlike a Traditional IRA, you pay taxes on your contributions now, but in retirement you can withdraw everything—including all your earnings—without paying any taxes.

settings.card1Body: For example: churches; denominational headquarters or councils; church-affiliated, tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organizations.
settings.card2Title: Others serving in a ministerial capacity

settings.title: Annual Contribution Limits
fineprint: *Beginning in 2026, participants who have FICA wages exceeding $150,000 (adjusted for inflation) in the previous calendar year will be required to make any catch-up contributions on a Roth (after-tax) basis. It is the Employer’s responsibility to ensure contributions are correctly submitted to the Plan. Employees below the $150,000 threshold, as well as ministers who earn SECA wages may continue to make catch-up contributions on either a pre-tax or Roth basis, depending on your plan’s design.

**The rule applies to individuals who will attain age 60 in the taxable year and continues until the taxable year in which they turn 64. So, a participant would be eligible for the entire year in which they turn 60 (even if their birthday is December 31), and they would not be eligible in the year in which they turn 64.
***All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax. Cannot exceed includible compensation.

†All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax; amounts over the general overall limit must be age 50 catch-up deferrals. Cannot exceed includible compensation except to the extent that the age 50 or older catch-up deferral has been utilized.

Contact your own tax advisor before taking any action that would have a tax consequence. This information is not tax advice. Information is from sources deemed reliable. Information is subject to error, omission, withdrawal, or change.
settings.card1Bullets:
Under age 50 deferral limit (pre-tax and Roth after-tax): The lesser of $24,500 or includible compensation.

Age 60-63 deferral limit**: The lesser of $35,750 or includible compensation.
Overall limit under age 50***: $72,000
Overall limit age 50 and up†: $80,000
Overall limit age 60-63**: $83,250
settings.card2Bullets:
Under age 50 deferral limit (pre-tax and Roth after-tax): The lesser of $23,500 or includible compensation.
Age 50 and up deferral limit*: The lesser of $31,000 or includible compensation.
Age 60-63 deferral limit**: The lesser of $34,750 or includible compensation.
Overall limit under age 50***: $70,000
Overall limit age 50 and up†: $77,500
Overall limit age 60-63**: $81,250

settings.title: Start enrollment
settings.card2Title: Establish a plan as an employer.

settings.html:
403(b) Plan Loans

A 403(b) loan allows you to borrow money from your own retirement savings without incurring early withdrawal tax penalties. The interest paid on this type of loan goes back into your retirement savings. Though convenient, this type of loan can significantly impact your retirement savings growth.

Details

The requested 403(b) loan amount cannot be less than $1,500. In addition, the amount borrowed cannot exceed the lesser of:

  • 100% of the total vested account balance if less than $10,000
  • 50% of the total vested account balances
  • or $50,000

Contact your AGFinancial retirement consultant for more information.

Members may have no more than two loans at a time. The interest rate for plan loans is fixed for the life of the loan at 2.0% above the rate of the MBA Income Fund. All loan payments are made by automatic bank draft on the 20th of each month. The maximum term of a loan is 59 months (5 years) regardless of intended use.

Due to regulations issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, 403(b) plan loans issued after Dec. 31, 2008 require employer verification of loan qualifications with the following exception: your employer has a sole service provider agreement with Ministers Benefit Association, and has not had multiple service providers since 2004.

settings.title: How to apply
settings.card1Body: Review the loan rules.
settings.card2Body: Log in.
settings.card4Body: Click **Manage My Retirement** under **Retirement Details**.
settings.card5Body: Select your plan and open the **Info** tab.
settings.card6Body: Under **Take Action On Your Account**, select **Loans**, and then **Request a Loan**.

settings.heading: Ministry-powered retirement.
settings.bodyHtml: The AGFinancial 403(b) is designed specifically for ministers and ministry employees. It’s a powerful way to save while you serve.
settings.body: The AGFinancial 403(b) is designed specifically for ministers and ministry employees. It’s a powerful way to save while you serve.

settings.title: Benefits you’ll love.
settings.card1Body: The AGFinancial flagship fixed income investment option provides a fixed rate of return, and helps build churches and ministry facilities.
settings.card2Body: This unique investment option ensures the securities you own are aligned with biblical ethical standards.
settings.card3Body: This significant tax-saving benefit is available to retired ministers through the AGFinancial 403(b) plan.
settings.card4Body: This option allows taxes to be paid on the contribution now, in order to provide tax-free withdrawals at retirement.
settings.card5Body: Retirement savings can be simplified by consolidating other retirement accounts into a single 403(b).
settings.card6Body: Investment options include low-cost index funds, actively-managed funds, risk-based and target-date strategies, and individual funds.
settings.card7Body: Our regional consultants are available to answer your questions, help customize your plan, and assist you with implementation.
settings.card8Body: Onsite education for your participants is available, and includes retirement trends, IRS regulations, and customized action plans.

settings.card1Body: AGFinancial’s flagship fund pays a fixed rate declared quarterly, with interest compounding monthly. Your investment is used to provide loans to build churches and ministry facilities across the country.
settings.card2Body: These pre-mixed strategies are based on risk tolerance levels, and create a diversified portfolio with a single investment choice.
settings.card3Body: Based on your target date of retirement, these screened strategies automatically adjust to become more conservative as your target date approaches.
settings.card4Body: This option creates a fully custom-built portfolio designed specifically for you and your retirement goals.

settings.title: Who qualifies for the AGFinancial 403(b)?
settings.card1Body: For example: churches; denominational headquarters or councils; church-affiliated, tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organizations.
settings.card2Title: Others serving in a ministerial capacity
settings.card2Body: Such as a chaplain, campus pastor, or counselor in a non-ministry organization.
settings.card3Body: Such as pastors, evangelists, or independent ministry leaders.

settings.title: Annual Contribution Limits
fineprint: *Beginning in 2026, participants who have FICA wages exceeding $150,000 (adjusted for inflation) in the previous calendar year will be required to make any catch-up contributions on a Roth (after-tax) basis. It is the Employer’s responsibility to ensure contributions are correctly submitted to the Plan. Employees below the $150,000 threshold, as well as ministers who earn SECA wages may continue to make catch-up contributions on either a pre-tax or Roth basis, depending on your plan’s design.

**The rule applies to individuals who will attain age 60 in the taxable year and continues until the taxable year in which they turn 64. So, a participant would be eligible for the entire year in which they turn 60 (even if their birthday is December 31), and they would not be eligible in the year in which they turn 64.
***All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax. Cannot exceed includible compensation.

†All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax; amounts over the general overall limit must be age 50 catch-up deferrals. Cannot exceed includible compensation except to the extent that the age 50 or older catch-up deferral has been utilized.

Contact your own tax advisor before taking any action that would have a tax consequence. This information is not tax advice. Information is from sources deemed reliable. Information is subject to error, omission, withdrawal, or change.

settings.title: Start enrollment
settings.card2Title: Establish a plan as an employer.

settings.html:
403(b) Plan Loans

A 403(b) loan allows you to borrow money from your own retirement savings without incurring early withdrawal tax penalties. The interest paid on this type of loan goes back into your retirement savings. Though convenient, this type of loan can significantly impact your retirement savings growth.

Details

The requested 403(b) loan amount cannot be less than $1,500. In addition, the amount borrowed cannot exceed the lesser of:

  • 100% of the total vested account balance if less than $10,000
  • 50% of the total vested account balances
  • or $50,000

Contact your AGFinancial retirement consultant for more information.

Members may have no more than two loans at a time. The interest rate for plan loans is fixed for the life of the loan at 2.0% above the rate of the MBA Income Fund. All loan payments are made by automatic bank draft on the 20th of each month. The maximum term of a loan is 59 months (5 years) regardless of intended use.

Due to regulations issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, 403(b) plan loans issued after Dec. 31, 2008 require employer verification of loan qualifications with the following exception: your employer has a sole service provider agreement with Ministers Benefit Association, and has not had multiple service providers since 2004.

settings.title: How to apply
settings.card1Body: Review the loan rules.
settings.card2Body: Log in.
settings.card4Body: Click **Manage My Retirement** under **Retirement Details**.
settings.card5Body: Select your plan and open the **Info** tab.
settings.card6Body: Under **Take Action On Your Account**, select **Loans**, and then **Request a Loan**.

settings.title: Annual Contribution Limits
fineprint: *Beginning in 2026, participants who have FICA wages exceeding $150,000 (adjusted for inflation) in the previous calendar year will be required to make any catch-up contributions on a Roth (after-tax) basis. It is the Employer’s responsibility to ensure contributions are correctly submitted to the Plan. Employees below the $150,000 threshold, as well as ministers who earn SECA wages may continue to make catch-up contributions on either a pre-tax or Roth basis, depending on your plan’s design.

**The rule applies to individuals who will attain age 60 in the taxable year and continues until the taxable year in which they turn 64. So, a participant would be eligible for the entire year in which they turn 60 (even if their birthday is December 31), and they would not be eligible in the year in which they turn 64.
***All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax. Cannot exceed includible compensation.

†All types of contributions including deferrals, employer, and traditional after-tax; amounts over the general overall limit must be age 50 catch-up deferrals. Cannot exceed includible compensation except to the extent that the age 50 or older catch-up deferral has been utilized.

Contact your own tax advisor before taking any action that would have a tax consequence. This information is not tax advice. Information is from sources deemed reliable. Information is subject to error, omission, withdrawal, or change.

settings.title: Start enrollment
settings.card2Title: Establish a plan as an employer.

settings.html:
403(b) Plan Loans

A 403(b) loan allows you to borrow money from your own retirement savings without incurring early withdrawal tax penalties. The interest paid on this type of loan goes back into your retirement savings. Though convenient, this type of loan can significantly impact your retirement savings growth.

Details

The requested 403(b) loan amount cannot be less than $1,500. In addition, the amount borrowed cannot exceed the lesser of:

  • 100% of the total vested account balance if less than $10,000
  • 50% of the total vested account balances
  • or $50,000

Contact your AGFinancial retirement consultant for more information.

Members may have no more than two loans at a time. The interest rate for plan loans is fixed for the life of the loan at 2.0% above the rate of the MBA Income Fund. All loan payments are made by automatic bank draft on the 20th of each month. The maximum term of a loan is 59 months (5 years) regardless of intended use.

Due to regulations issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, 403(b) plan loans issued after Dec. 31, 2008 require employer verification of loan qualifications with the following exception: your employer has a sole service provider agreement with Ministers Benefit Association, and has not had multiple service providers since 2004.

settings.title: How to apply
settings.card1Body: Review the loan rules.
settings.card2Body: Log in.
settings.card4Body: Click **Manage My Retirement** under **Retirement Details**.
settings.card5Body: Select your plan and open the **Info** tab.
settings.card6Body: Under **Take Action On Your Account**, select **Loans**, and then **Request a Loan**.

settings.title: A rollover is easy. Smart, too.
settings.bodyHtml: Rolling over your scattered retirement savings into a single AGFinancial 403(b) is surprisingly simple…and undeniably smart. One account. One login.

settings.col2BodyHtml: This unique IRS benefit, which gives ministers a significant tax savings, is not available through secular 403(b) plans or IRAs. It allows retired ministers to have distributions from the AGFinancial 403(b) plan designated as clergy housing allowance.

settings.col1Body: This online tool for employer contributions will help minimize monthly data entry and maximize accuracy as you make retirement contributions on behalf of your employees.

settings.heading: Most wealth isn’t cash.
settings.bodyHtml:
It’s assets. A Ministry Impact Fund® makes it easy for donors to support your ministry with non-cash gifts. No administrative hassle—just streamlined generosity that expands giving options, maximizes tax deductions, and eliminates capital gains.

This is generosity without limits.
settings.body:
It’s assets. A Ministry Impact Fund® makes it easy for donors to give in any form. No administrative hassle—just streamlined generosity that expands giving options, maximizes tax deductions, and eliminates capital gains.

This is generosity without limits.

settings.title: How it works
settings.col1Body: Open a Ministry Impact Fund®. Your donors transfer cash or assets to the fund, potentially a charitable deduction and minimized or eliminated capital gains.
settings.col2Body: AG Foundation liquidates the assets for you and your donors, handling all administrative details.
settings.col3Body: Your ministry gains immediate access to the cash.

settings.heading: Your IRA can do more.
settings.bodyHtml: If you're 70½ or older, a Qualified Charitable Distribution (QCD) lets you transfer up to $110,000 per year directly to your church or an eligible ministry — tax-free, and straight from the source. It counts toward your required minimum distribution, and not a dollar goes to taxes first.
settings.body: If you're 70½ or older, a Qualified Charitable Distribution (QCD) lets you transfer up to $110,000 per year directly to your church or an eligible ministry — tax-free, and straight from the source. It counts toward your required minimum distribution, and not a dollar goes to taxes first.

settings.title: How it works
settings.col1Body: Tell your IRA administrator you'd like to make a QCD. They will initiate the direct transfer.
settings.col2Body: Choose where the gift goes—a church, a ministry, a 501(c)(3) organization—and decide the amount.
settings.col3Body: Because the distribution goes directly to the ministry, it's excluded from your taxable income entirely. Your generosity goes further.

settings.heading: Create an enduring legacy.
settings.bodyHtml:
Your endowment is a gift that gives forever. The interest earnings from your carefully-invested donation support your chosen ministry or cause. Meanwhile, your original gift stays protected and continues to grow.

This generosity never runs out.
settings.body:
Your endowment is a gift that gives forever. The interest earnings from your carefully-invested donation support your chosen ministry or cause. Meanwhile, your original gift stays protected and continues to grow.

This generosity never runs out.

settings.title: How it works
settings.col1Body: Designated assets are invested to ensure their protection and growth.
settings.col2Body: Payments are made from ongoing interest earned from the gifted asset(s).
settings.col3Body: An endowment requires that the principal remain intact indefinitely—or until sufficient assets have accumulated to ensure the endowment’s perpetuity.

settings.title: It starts with what you give.
settings.card1Fineprint: Minimum funding requirements are $10,000 for cash or securities, and $100,000 for real estate.

settings.title: See how your endowment can keep giving.
Let's get started.
settings.body: Building your endowment begins with a conversation. We’re ready to help you explore how your gift can continue to give. And give. And give…

settings.title: It starts with what you give.
settings.card1Fineprint: Minimum funding requirements are $10,000 for cash or securities, and $100,000 for real estate.

settings.heading:
Tax benefits.
Ministry support.
Payments for life.
settings.bodyHtml: ...and payments that won't change with the market. Through a Charitable Gift Annuity (CGA), your generosity has the power to bless both the ministries and the people you love with fixed payments, charitable tax deductions, and attractive rates.
settings.body: ...and completely unaffected by the economy. Through a Charitable Gift Annuity (CGA), your generosity has the power to bless both the ministries and the people you love with fixed payments, potential tax deductions, and attractive rates.

settings.title: How it works
settings.col1Body: You fund the gift with cash or securities, and should receive an immediate charitable deduction.
settings.col2Body: AG Foundation invests those assets and pays you a fixed amount (according to your age) every year for the rest of your life.
settings.col3Body: When you pass away, a portion of the remainder goes to support ministry.

settings.title: It starts with your gift.
settings.card1Body:
• Cash (a significant portion of the annuity income may be tax-free)
  • Appreciated securities (may avoid a portion of capital gains tax)
  • $10,000 minimum

The SECURE 2.0 Act allows you to fund a Charitable Gift Annuity with funds distributed from your IRA up to $50,000* of your annual Qualified Charitable Distribution limit (QCD). This charitable distribution amount is both retirement income for you, and a gift of support to a ministry you choose. Even better, this distribution can count toward your IRA’s annual Required Minimum Distribution (RMD). You’re permitted to take advantage of this unique opportunity only once.

settings.html: The SECURE 2.0 Act allows you to fund a Charitable Gift Annuity with funds distributed from your IRA up to $50,000* of your annual Qualified Charitable Distribution limit (QCD). This charitable distribution amount is both retirement income for you, and a gift of support to a ministry you choose. Even better, this distribution can count toward your IRA’s annual Required Minimum Distribution (RMD). You’re permitted to take advantage of this unique opportunity only once.
Also available for Charitable Remainder Unitrust (CRUT) or Charitable Remainder Annuity Trust (CRAT).
settings.fineprint:
*Indexed annually for inflation
**Also available for Charitable Remainder Unitrust (CRUT) or Charitable Remainder Annuity Trust (CRAT)
This is a one-time, lifetime opportunity; not available on an annual basis
Restrictions apply.

settings.title: Charitable Gift Annuity Options
settings.card1Body:
Start receiving payments **now**.

If you desire current income, you may transfer cash or securities in exchange for a contract for payment to begin within four weeks. You should receive a current income tax charitable deduction for the value of your gift to AG Foundation.
settings.card2Body:
Receive payments in the **future**.

Deferment compresses payout into a shorter time frame, so your annual payments will be higher than an immediate CGA. You should receive a current charitable income tax deduction.

settings.title: Your gifts are more powerful than you think.
settings.body: When you’re ready for tax deductions, fixed payments, and attractive rates—all while supporting ministry—we’re ready to walk you through the setup process.

settings.title: Plenty of options.
settings.subtitle: Explore other charitable and planned giving strategies.

settings.fineprint:
Except for California, your Assemblies of God Charitable Gift Annuity will be issued by Assemblies of God Foundation (“AG Foundation”) and will be a general obligation of the organization. Charitable Gift Annuities are not available in Alabama, Hawaii, Montana, New Jersey, New York, or Washington.

Additional information for California residents: Annuities are subject to regulation by the State of California. Payments under this agreement, however, are not protected or otherwise guaranteed by any government agency or the California Life and Health Insurance Guarantee Association. AG Foundation does not practice law and no legal advice is provided. If you need legal advice, you should consult your own legal counsel. Your Assemblies of God Charitable Gift Annuity will be issued by the General Council of the Assemblies of God (“General Council”) and will be a general obligation of that organization. AG Foundation is responsible for the management of your gift annuity.

Additional information for Oklahoma residents: A Charitable Gift Annuity is not regulated by the Oklahoma Insurance Department and is not protected by a guaranty association with the Oklahoma Insurance Department.

Additional information for South Dakota residents: Charitable Gift Annuities are not regulated by and are not under the jurisdiction of the South Dakota Division of Insurance.
